--- gd-head-tags: - >- ``{=html} open-graph: title: >- [Graph.local_and_global_consistency()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} | EdgeCase description: >- Predict missing node labels with the local and global consistency method. twitter-card: title: >- [Graph.local_and_global_consistency()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} | EdgeCase description: >- Predict missing node labels with the local and global consistency method. title: >- [Graph.local_and_global_consistency()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} body-classes: doc-api-page doc-py-api-page shift-heading-level-by: 0 bread-crumbs: false toc-depth: 3 description-meta: >- Predict missing node labels with the local and global consistency method. page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Predict missing node labels with the local and global consistency method. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/edgecase/blob/main/python/edgecase/graph.py#L46955-L47090){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-function} ```pythonsignature Graph.local_and_global_consistency( label_name, alpha=0.99, max_iter=30, weighted=None, ) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} ![Local and global consistency](../assets/graphs/local-and-global-consistency.light.svg){.lightbox fig-alt="Two dense four-node groups, A, B, C, D and E, F, G, H, joined by the edge D to E. Only A is labeled red and H blue, shown as badges. Spreading the labels with the normalized adjacency, each node mixing its neighbors' scores with its own start, predicts red (accent color) for A, B, C, D and blue (teal) for E, F, G, H, as the card lists; both seeds keep their labels." width="100%"} Like `harmonic_function()`, this spreads a few known labels (in the node attribute `label_name`) over the network to classify the remaining nodes, but it lets the known labels themselves be smoothed too. Each node's scores mix what its neighbors say (weight `alpha`) with its own initial label (weight `1 - alpha`), using a symmetrically normalized adjacency, so noisy labels can be overruled by a strongly connected neighborhood (Zhou et al., 2004). The graph must be undirected. ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [label_name]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [str]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Node attribute holding the known labels; nodes without it (or with `None`) are unlabeled. As with `harmonic_function()`, this can't be the `label` column of node names. [alpha]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [float]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[0.99]{.fl}]{.doc-parameter-default} : How much each node listens to its neighbors versus its own initial label, between 0 and 1 (default 0.99). [max_iter]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [int]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[30]{.dv}]{.doc-parameter-default} : Number of propagation steps (default 30). [weighted]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [bool | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Whether to propagate along edge weights. If `None` (default), follows the graph's `weighted` flag. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [dict]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : The predicted label of every node, keyed by node ID. Unlike `harmonic_function()`, a labeled node can receive a different label. ::: ## Raises {.doc-raises} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [ValueError]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If the graph is directed or no node is labeled. ::: ## Technical Notes {.doc-technical-notes} With $S = D^{-1/2} A D^{-1/2}$ and one-hot labels $Y$, $F \leftarrow \alpha S F + (1 - \alpha) Y$ is iterated `max_iter` times from $F = 0$; it converges to $(1 - \alpha)(I - \alpha S)^{-1} Y$. This is NetworkX's `local_and_global_consistency` exactly (exact ties go to the class seen first). ## See Also {.doc-see-also} [](`~harmonic_function`) : Spread known labels, holding them fixed. [](`~cmty_label_propagation`) : Spread labels with none known in advance. ## Examples {.doc-examples} Two triangles joined by a single edge, with one node of each labeled in the `group` attribute. Each label spreads over its own triangle: ::: {#f6b0703b .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec graph = ec.Graph.from_edges([ ("A", "B"), ("B", "C"), ("C", "A"), ("C", "D"), ("D", "E"), ("E", "F"), ("F", "D"), ]) graph.set_node_attrs("group", {"A": "red", "F": "blue"}) predicted = graph.local_and_global_consistency(label_name="group") {graph.get_label_from_id(n): group for n, group in predicted.items()} ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` {'A': 'red', 'B': 'red', 'C': 'red', 'D': 'blue', 'E': 'blue', 'F': 'blue'} ``` ::: ::: ### Two labels from the edge of the club Zachary's karate club split in two after a dispute between its instructor (member 0) and its administrator (member 33), and the `faction` attribute records which side each member joined. Giving the faction of members 16 and 26 only, both on the edge of the club, `harmonic_function()` misplaces six of the instructor's friends. Local and global consistency misplaces only member 2, who has friends on both sides: ::: {#26950493 .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} import polars as pl karate = ec.karate_club().layout_kamada_kawai() karate.set_node_attrs("known", {"16": 1, "26": 2}) harmonic = karate.harmonic_function(label_name="known") lgc = karate.local_and_global_consistency(label_name="known") karate.set_node_attrs("harmonic", harmonic).set_node_attrs("lgc", lgc) members = karate.get_node_df() def misplaced(column): wrong = members.filter(pl.col(column) != pl.col("faction")) return wrong["label"].to_list() misplaced("harmonic"), misplaced("lgc") ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ``` (['1', '2', '3', '7', '13', '19'], ['2']) ``` ::: ::: The labeled members are drawn larger: ::: {#bcb34f48 .cell execution_count=3} ``` {.python .cell-code} karate.set_node_attrs("size", 1) karate.set_node_attrs("size", 2, nodes=["16", "26"]) karate.plot( layout="pos", color_by="lgc", size_by="size", label_by="label" ) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=3} ```{=html}
``` ::: ::: ### How much to listen to the neighbors `alpha=` sets how much each node's scores come from its neighbors rather than its own starting label. With a low `alpha`, a label barely spreads beyond the labeled members' neighborhoods, and more members are placed wrong: ::: {#1b76468f .cell execution_count=4} ``` {.python .cell-code} rows = [] for alpha in (0.1, 0.5, 0.9, 0.99): guess = karate.local_and_global_consistency( label_name="known", alpha=alpha ) karate.set_node_attrs("guess", guess) members = karate.get_node_df() wrong = members.filter(pl.col("guess") != pl.col("faction")).height rows.append({"alpha": alpha, "wrong": wrong}) pl.DataFrame(rows) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=4} ```{=html}
